lessons.title: How Green Leaves Feed Our Crops
lessons.summary: Learn the role of chlorophyll, sunlight, and water in sustaining life on earth.
lessons.content:
Photosynthesis is nature's kitchen inside every green leaf. The word comes from 'Photo' (light) and 'Synthesis' (putting together). 

Plants absorb water through roots from the soil, capture carbon dioxide from the air through tiny openings called stomata, and use sunlight caught by green chlorophyll pigment to produce glucose (sugar) and oxygen.

Equation in simple terms:
Sunlight + Carbon Dioxide + Water -> Glucose (Energy for plant) + Oxygen (Breath for us).
keyPoints: Chlorophyll gives leaves their green color and traps solar rays.
Stomata are microscopic pores on the underside of leaves.
Oxygen is released as a vital byproduct that humans and animals breathe.
During the night, plants pause photosynthesis and mainly respire.
lessons.practicalExample: Think of paddy fields in the morning sun: when leaves spread wide, they are soaking up sunlight like solar cookers to grow healthy grain ears.
lessons.ruralContextNote: Farmers notice crops growing slower during persistent cloudy monsoon weeks because less sunlight reaches chlorophyll to power glucose production.

lessons.title: Dividing Field Harvests Fairly
lessons.summary: Mastering numerators and denominators through physical land division.
lessons.content:
A fraction represents part of a whole quantity. The top number is the Numerator (how many pieces you take) and the bottom number is the Denominator (how many equal pieces the whole was divided into).

When two neighbors share 1 bag of organic seeds equally, each gets 1/2 (one-half). If divided among 4 farming families, each gets 1/4 (one-fourth).
keyPoints: Numerator = selected parts; Denominator = total equal pieces.
Equal size is essential: 1/4 means four strictly identical shares.
Equivalent fractions: 2/4 is the exact same amount as 1/2.
lessons.practicalExample: If a farmer has 8 sacks of wheat and keeps 2 sacks for the family while selling 6 sacks at the weekly mandi (market), the family keeps 2/8 (or 1/4) of the harvest.
lessons.ruralContextNote: Used every day in traditional land sharing (Batta / Adhi system) and measuring pond irrigation water shares.

questions.prompt: Which green pigment in leaves captures energy from sunlight?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plant cells that traps solar energy needed to drive photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: What gas do plants take in from the atmosphere to carry out photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Leaves absorb Carbon Dioxide (CO2) through microscopic pores called stomata.

questions.prompt: What essential gas is released into the air as a byproduct of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Oxygen (O2) is split from water molecules and released into the air for humans and animals to breathe.

questions.prompt: Why do crops grow slower during prolonged cloudy monsoon weeks?
options: Reduced sunlight decreases the rate of photosynthesis
The soil loses all nitrogen instantly
Plants sleep all day when cloudy
questions.explanation: Sunlight is the fundamental energy source; without sufficient light, the photosynthetic machinery cannot manufacture enough glucose.

questions.prompt: In the fraction 3/5, what is the number 5 called and what does it represent?
options: Denominator: the total number of equal parts
questions.explanation: The bottom number is the denominator, which shows how many equal parts make up the complete whole.

questions.prompt: A farmer divides 12 bighas of land equally among 3 children. What fraction of the total land does each child receive?
questions.explanation: Dividing any whole among 3 equal recipients gives 1/3 to each.
Dividing both numerator and denominator by 2 simplifies 2/4 to 1/2.
